ai.title: Serum Lactate Dehydrogenase in Paediatrics
ai.subject: Paediatrics
ai.summary: LDH is a cytoplasmic enzyme released on cell injury. In children it flags hemolysis, tissue necrosis or tumour burden. Interpretation must consider local disease patterns and test availability.

b: Enzyme present in all cells; released on injury
sections.p: LDH is an intracellular enzyme converting lactate to pyruvate. Serum elevation indicates cell turnover or damage. Reference range 140–280 U/L in most labs; local ranges may differ.

t.b: Elevated LDH suggests hemolysis, myocarditis, sepsis, tumour, or tissue necrosis; normal LDH does not exclude disease if other markers are abnormal.

b: >500 U/L – marked elevation, consider tumour or severe infection
sections.p: LDH is not a staging tool alone but correlates with disease burden. In haemolytic anaemias, a 2–3 fold rise is significant; in malignancy, >500 U/L may indicate high tumour load.

b: Hemolysis – malaria, sickle cell, G6PD deficiency
Other – TB, hepatitis B, herbal remedies
sections.p: In East Africa, the top causes of raised LDH in children are hemolysis, sepsis, malaria, and tumour. Other contributors include sickle cell crisis, TB, and herbal nephrotoxicity.

Raised LDH is usually silent; it is inferred from clinical context: jaundice, pallor, fever, lymphadenopathy, or unexplained anaemia. It may accompany other lab abnormalities such as low haptoglobin or high bilirubin.
LDH is a screening marker; confirm the underlying cause with targeted tests. When LDH is high, look for hemolysis, infection, or tumour.

t.b: Schistocytes suggest mechanical hemolysis; parasites confirm malaria.

b: Acute kidney injury – monitor urine output
sections.p: Severe LDH elevation with haemolysis can lead to acute kidney injury, hypovolaemia, and shock. In tumour, it may herald tumour lysis syndrome.

Treat the underlying cause first. Supportive care includes transfusion for severe anaemia, antibiotics for sepsis, antimalarials for malaria, and chemotherapy for lymphoma. Monitor LDH to gauge response.
Repeat LDH every 48–72 hours in acute settings. Prevent malaria with bed nets, treat sickle cell with hydroxyurea, and counsel on safe herbal use.
Elevated LDH can mimic other conditions: high AST/ALT in liver disease, or high CK in rhabdomyolysis. Context and additional tests differentiate them.

b: Early haemolysis – LDH may still be normal
sections.p: LDH can be falsely normal in early haemolysis or low in chronic disease. Interfering substances (hemolysis of sample) can spuriously raise LDH.
